points.t: A **ring-shaped** rash: first decide **scaly or smooth**, and whether the **edge or the inside** carries the scale.
Different engines share a ring: **dermatophytes** (tinea), **psoriasis**, **dermal granulomas** (GA), **reactive** eruptions (PR, EAC).
**Mycology scrape** if tinea is plausible, then treat the cause; review a solitary lesion in 1 week.
**Erythema migrans** after a tick bite; **SCLE** (photosensitive, new drug); fixed plaques in older adults → biopsy (lymphoma).

points: **Granuloma annulare**: dermal granulomatous inflammation; often idiopathic.
**EAC**: reactive figurate erythema; hunt triggers (infection, drugs, rarely malignancy).
**Tinea**: active raised **scaly edge**, central clearing, asymmetric; pets / soil; feet / nails reservoir.
**Annular psoriasis**: silvery scale, may be symmetric; other plaques, nails, scalp.
**GA**: **smooth, non-scaly** beaded rings; dorsal hands / feet, ankles.
**PR herald**: oval with **collarette**; Christmas-tree rash follows.
**EAC**: **trailing scale inside** a slowly advancing edge; trunk / thighs.

visuals.caption: Granuloma annulare (left): a smooth ring of skin-coloured beaded papules, no scale. Tinea (right): red ring with a raised scaly active edge and central clearing.
visuals.alt: Two hands comparing a smooth beaded ring with a scaly ring

visuals.caption: Where is the scale? PR collarette lies just inside the edge; tinea scale sits on the advancing outer edge.

points: **Mycology before prolonged steroid**: the single most useful primary-care test.
Pets, steroids used, herald then cascade, joints / nails, tick bite / Lyme geography.
Solitary lesion: 1 week (PR secondary rash or tinea expansion).

points: Psoriasis: NICE topical pathway. EAC: treat trigger; topical steroid; dermatology if persistent.
**Topical terbinafine or imidazole** (duration per BNF); oral terbinafine if extensive / failed (interactions, LFTs); treat the foot reservoir.
Reassure (6–12 weeks); emollient ± mild–moderate steroid; atypical → syphilis serology / dermatology.
Localised: observe; topical steroid / tacrolimus sometimes; extensive → dermatology.

limits.k: Potent steroid on an undiagnosed ring

items.t: Expanding ring after a tick bite: **erythema migrans**, treat clinically (NG95).
Photosensitive annular plaques with systemic features or a new drug (PPI, terbinafine, thiazide): **SCLE**.
Persistent fixed non-healing annular plaques in an older adult: biopsy (cutaneous lymphoma).

pearls.t: Scale on the **outside edge** → tinea; **inside** → PR / EAC; **no scale** → GA.
Never use potent steroid long term on an undiagnosed ring.
Check feet and nails whenever you diagnose body tinea.
